trends.name: Iran War Escalation & Oil Surge
trends.summary: US oil prices surged above $105/barrel (+22% since Wednesday) as Trump threatens to hit Iran's energy sites and escalate military efforts to reopen Strait of Hormuz. Netanyahu confirms US spearheading military efforts while uncertainty over peace timeline persists. Maritime shipping corridors remain under threat with UKMTO warnings active.

trends.name: Semiconductor Sector Underperformance vs Software
trends.summary: Software outperformed semiconductors by 500+ basis points (5%) in a single day—a rare event occurring only 0-2 times in the past 3 months. Micron sank 10% post-earnings, signaling weakness in chip demand amid broader tech volatility. This rare sector rotation reflects investor concerns about AI capex economics.

trends.name: Unilever-McCormick Food Industry Mega-Deal
trends.summary: Unilever nearing ~$60 billion deal to combine food business with McCormick, creating massive food giant with ~$16 billion cash component. Expected announcement as early as Tuesday. Reflects consolidation trend in food distribution sector alongside Sysco's $29 billion Restaurant Depot acquisition.

trends.name: Nasdaq Weakness & Market Volatility Spike
trends.summary: Nasdaq on pace for second 3-day streak of 1%+ declines already in 2026. S&P 500 extended losing streak with oil settlement above $100/barrel. US stocks underperforming historically during geopolitical shocks with room to fall further. Suggests growing risk-off sentiment despite occasional peace deal rumors.

trends.name: Strait of Hormuz Blockade & Supply Chain Risk
trends.summary: Ongoing maritime security threats with UKMTO warnings active and shipping carriers reporting direct Iran war impact. China exporting diesel to Southeast Asia signaling energy shortages. Global supply chains face disruption risk; Sysco, JetBlue and other logistics firms raising prices to offset fuel/shipping costs.

trends.name: China Manufacturing Recovery & Export Concerns
trends.summary: China's factory activity returns to growth at sharpest pace in a year, signaling economic rebound. However, Strait of Hormuz closure threatens export prices—suppliers warning of higher prices for Americans. China's strategic fuel exports to Southeast Asia reflect geopolitical repositioning amid US-Iran tensions.

trends.name: Retail Consumer Weakness & Spending Pullback
trends.summary: Most Americans have already received tax refunds early, depriving restaurants and retailers of expected Q2 spending boost. Combined with rising costs (airline bag fees, streaming costs exceeding $1,200 for sports), consumer discretionary spending faces headwinds. Timing mismatch creates near-term retail weakness.

trends.name: Treasury Selling by Oil-Producing Nations
trends.summary: Middle East's major oil-producing countries actively selling US Treasurys amid Iran war escalation and oil price surge. Reflects diversification away from dollar assets and potential hedge against US military spending. Could pressure long-term US bond yields and dollar strength.

trends.name: Fiduciary Rule Collapse & Retirement Investor Impact
trends.summary: Retirement saver protection rule has died for the second time, removing guardrails against conflicted investment advice. Investors face increased risk of fee-laden, advisor-recommended products without fiduciary obligations. Creates regulatory vacuum in wealth management industry.

trends.name: AI Power Infrastructure Demand Questions
trends.summary: Trump-named AI power company projects show no customer pipeline despite significant hype. Raises questions about actual enterprise demand for specialized AI power infrastructure beyond hyperscaler capex. Signals potential overestimation of AI-driven infrastructure spending cycle.

trends.name: Airline Cost Pressures & Fee Escalation
trends.summary: JetBlue raising checked bag fees by at least $4 as fuel prices soar above $105/barrel. Airlines facing compressed margins from geopolitical oil shock with limited ability to pass costs fully to consumers. Expect broader industry fee increases across carriers.

trends.name: Sysco Restaurant Depot Consolidation Play
trends.summary: Sysco nearing $29 billion acquisition of family-owned Restaurant Depot, doubling down on cash-and-carry food service model. Strategic move to consolidate fragmented foodservice distribution ahead of inflationary cost pressures. Largest deal signals confidence in restaurant sector consolidation thesis despite near-term consumer headwinds.
